title: Catalyst Canvas Brief
challenge: A nonprofit needs a clearer way to explain program impact to funders without overstating certainty.

audience.primary: Program director at a community nonprofit

goal: Build a defensible impact story with traceable indicators

constraints.statement: Limited data, small team capacity, and stakeholder pressure for simple results

personas.name: Program director at a community nonprofit
personas.description: Needs help addressing: A nonprofit needs a clearer way to explain program impact to funders without overstating certainty.. The user wants build a defensible impact story with traceable indicators while navigating limited data, small team capacity, and stakeholder pressure for simple results.
needs: Build a defensible impact story with traceable indicators
pains: Limited data, small team capacity, and stakeholder pressure for simple results

point_of_view.statement: Program director at a community nonprofit needs a practical way to address 'A nonprofit needs a clearer way to explain program impact to funders without overstating certainty.' so they can build a defensible impact story with traceable indicators without ignoring the constraint: Limited data, small team capacity, and stakeholder pressure for simple results.

how_might_we.question: How might we help Program director at a community nonprofit make the challenge concrete enough to act on?
How might we turn the goal — Build a defensible impact story with traceable indicators — into a small testable experiment?
How might we make the constraint visible without letting it stop progress?
How might we document assumptions so the next decision can be reviewed?

prompts.label: I want to
prompts.question: What progress is the user trying to make?

prompts.label: Constraint
prompts.question: What prevents the user from making progress today?

assumptions.statement: The stated audience is the right primary user for the first iteration.
The goal is specific enough to test with a small prototype.
The constraint is material and should remain visible in the design process.
A lightweight brief can reduce ambiguity before heavier implementation work begins.

prototypes.title: Reviewable Canvas Brief
prototypes.description: A one-page working artifact that captures the challenge, audience, goal, constraints, point of view, HMW prompts, prototype concept, assumptions, and test plan.

tests.title: Stakeholder clarity review
tests.signal: A stakeholder can explain the problem, proposed next step, and key assumption in their own words.
tests.method: Share the brief with 3–5 users or reviewers and capture confusion, objections, missing evidence, and next-step clarity.
tests.learning_goal: Determine whether the framing is clear enough to guide a real prototype or decision.

review_notes.note: What claim in this brief needs stronger evidence?
What assumption would most change the next step if it proved false?
What user signal would show that the prototype is worth continuing?
What should be rewritten to avoid overpromising?
